_comment: Reference test vectors for the safekey algorithm (docs/SAFEKEY.md). Phase 0 ships 13 vectors as a placeholder; the full set of 100 is a Phase 0 deliverable per docs/PHASES.md and is generated in coordination with BiblioFetch.jl. Format: each entry of `vectors[]` is { input: <ref string>, expected: <safekey> }. Both Rust and Julia implementations MUST produce identical output for every entry.
notes: Vectors are grouped by purpose: (1) basic DOI / arXiv mapping; (2) escape-collapse and trim-edge edge cases; (3) non-ASCII inputs.

Non-ASCII handling: algorithm step 1 replaces every char outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] with '_'. Since the result is pure ASCII before the byte-slice in the truncation branch, multibyte input cannot panic at `&trimmed[..192]`.

Collision caveat: refs that differ only in their non-ASCII suffix WILL collide on safekey output. This is a known consequence of the algorithm and a Phase-1 caller responsibility (cf. docs/SAFEKEY.md §6 property tests). The non-ASCII vectors below use distinct ASCII prefixes to keep the test suite collision-free.
